accounting.arithmetic: per call, the solver's RLIMIT_CPU (its timeout) plus 8.5 CPU-s: 3 generator RLIMIT_CPU + 2 x 1 loader-listing RLIMIT_CPU + 3 declared parent allowance + 0.25 reap + 0.25 settlement tail (the last two from SLAB-039's SUPERVISOR-POLICY.json). 8 x (50 + 8.5) + 4 x (15 + 8.5) = 468 + 94 = 562 CPU-s (by component: 460 CPU-s of solver limits + 102 CPU-s of per-call reserves)
accounting.binding_cap: the manifest cap, 600 CPU-s, binds: it is the tighter of the two. The room's 1,800 CPU-s prospective envelope does not bind. Neither is raised here; the final grant reconciles them.
accounting.host: x86_64 Azure host behind the mesh and TIMING evidence; an aarch64 build needs its own receipts
accounting.limits_lowered: to fit the true worst case under the 600 CPU-s cap (warden #56967 P2-3): the grid-64 timeout, and with it the solver's RLIMIT_CPU and wall deadline, from 60 to 50 s; the TAP generator's RLIMIT_CPU from 10 to 3 CPU-s and its wall deadline from 60 to 30 s. At 60 s the worst case would be 642 CPU-s.
accounting.worst_case_label: the true worst case from the limits: every child process (solver, generator, loader listings) runs under RLIMIT_CPU with soft = hard, so the kernel kills it at its limit; the parent's own CPU is a declared allowance, measured in every receipt and charged in full if exceeded; the hard cumulative process-group cap is the supervisor's

in_code_at_entry: manifest identity: validate-reference reads only CALL-LIST-v4.json and refuses it unless it is byte-identical to what this tree generates (the executed pins, every reference input and raw layout hash, the predicate, the limits, the accounting, the operator key and the anchor); the prior snapped manifest is refused

listed calls only: the call id with its listed --timeout, and the engine, reference and grid when given; before the manifest's window closes; on the listed architecture; on POSIX only, because the CPU limit is RLIMIT_CPU (Linux and macOS; Windows has no RLIMIT_CPU, and its equivalent, a Job Object process-time limit, is not implemented, so the entry refuses there); never under CI allocation (CI_ALLOCATION=1), where every native HotSpot launch goes through sundai_hotspot.ci_gate and SLAB-049 solves never run

accounting from the first step: the invocation's own and its children's CPU counters are read before any work, and every exit after admission is charged from there: the prechecks, both loader listings, the generator, the solver and the parent's own work

the operator's key and grant, before any work: the operator key (SLAB049_OPERATOR_KEY) must be the pinned public key's (a null pin refuses first, with no process work); the launch credential (SLAB049_ANCHOR_TOKEN) must be present; the signed, hash-chained ledger at the place derived from this manifest's id must verify, and its grant (entry 0) must name this manifest and this very ledger directory (a copy elsewhere is refused), with a cap no higher than 600 CPU-s

prechecks that only read files, before admission: identity markers and SHA-256 are read from a private content-addressed copy (mode 0500 in a 0700 directory), and that copy is the file executed; build provenance must describe exactly those bytes; a binary built with the CI entry guard is refused
raw geometry: the pinned raw layout hash (the vendored copy, and SLAB-048's record whenever it is in the tree) and the continuous rules only; the search lattice is never applied

the admission, one critical section for the grant (gate0_anchor.admit_and_reserve) before any process work, and the single place where the operator's authority is checked: under the ledger's lock, the grant's window (STOP once it has closed), the call's place in the grant, the operator's reserve tag, no ledger entry for the call and no earlier admission of it anywhere (the anchored admission chain); every admitted call is charged its envelope or its measured CPU if larger, and this call's envelope must fit the grant's cap; the window is checked again after those remote reads, before anything is created; then the chain's next place, admit-<NN>, is CREATED (create-only: two requests on any ledger or host can never both take one place, so no total passes the cap) and the signed reservation that binds it is appended. A create that returns after the cutoff stays consumed and charged and settles as window_closed before any process work; a call admitted in time keeps running. From then on the call is consumed and charged in full, never reclaimed and never retried, settle tag or not; no ledger deletion or rollback can readmit it. Any tag that cannot be read refuses: no admission on uncertainty

the process-capable precheck, inside the attempt: the shared libraries the binary's own loader resolves for the private copy must equal the build's (a mismatch settles the call as runtime_refused, charged), and they are listed again after the run (a change settles the call as runtime_changed)

the claim, immediately before launch: validate-reference CREATES gate0-<grant>/launch-<call> (create-only). Only a successful create launches; an existing ref refuses; an uncertain create (no answer after sending) consumes the call with no launch, for the operator to reconcile; nothing is retried from the absence of a settle tag

per-process CPU and wall limits on every child, soft = hard, so the kernel kills at the limit: the solver in its own session and process group at RLIMIT_CPU and a wall deadline both equal to its timeout, the group killed while the solver is unreaped, then the solver reaped; the TAP generator at 3 CPU-s and 30 s; each of the two loader listings at 1 CPU-s and 10 s, in its own session, killed as a group at its deadline

settlement: on every exit path after the admission, the signed receipt and the signed settlement entry, with the status, the CPU charged since the first step (children and self) and any overshoot; when no receipt can be written, the ledger still settles the call (receipt digest null). The settle tag's exact message, with the CPU charged, is printed for the operator

verification (record and report): by admitted call id from the signed ledger, never caller-chosen directories; every tag read by its exact name; every reservation anchored by its admission tag. A missing settle tag gives INCOMPLETE; a tag that cannot be read gives ERROR; a ledger, receipt or tag that does not verify or disagrees gives FAIL; a completed call is re-derived with the strict evaluator-bound reader. PASS needs all four required outcomes to agree everywhere and hold
operator_supervisor_contract: key custody: the operator's Ed25519 private key is generated and held by warden's supervisor and never enters the repository; its public key is pinned here (OPERATOR_PUBLIC_KEY) by a reviewed commit before the grant

the grant: the signed grant written as ledger entry 0 (gate0_anchor.open_ledger: grant id, call ids, window, CPU cap of at most 600 CPU-s) under the operator's ledger root; one grant per manifest (each grant has its own admission chain and cap); the root kept on storage the operator protects (append-only, backed up). Deleting or rolling it back cannot readmit an admitted call (the admission chain refuses), but it loses the evidence

the anchor: a repository ruleset on refs/tags/gate0-* that makes the namespace create-only (no update, no delete, no force-push, no bypass); reserve-<call> created before each launch; settle-<call> created after settlement with the printed message, failures included; a claim_uncertain call, or an admission whose create was uncertain, reconciled by settling it as a failure, never relaunched
credentials: SLAB049_ANCHOR_TOKEN (create tags in this repository) only in the supervisor's environment, never in the repository; GH_TOKEN with read access for record and report

a cumulative CPU budget over the whole process group, descendants and validate-reference itself included, enforced while calls run (for example a cgroup v2 budget that kills at the limit); in code, RLIMIT_CPU is per process and the parent's own CPU is measured and charged, not capped
kill and reap if validate-reference itself dies (SIGKILL, OOM, host loss): the call stays consumed (its admission and launch tags block any retry); settle it as unknown and charge its envelope

a protected runtime image: the loader, the libraries, the Python interpreter and its bytecode caches from immutable copies; in code, the executable is a private copy, but libraries are listed before and after the run, which cannot detect a swap-and-restore during it
a trusted clock for the grant window; the code reads the host clock
the final grant reconciles the 600 CPU-s manifest cap with the room's 1,800 CPU-s envelope; neither is raised here

source.derivation: Pinned: only what a call executes or reads (warden #56967 P2-4). (1) The TAP generator's repository files: slab049.trace_generator runs the generator exactly as validate-reference does, for both gate references, under a Python audit hook (sys.addaudithook) and lists every repository module it imports and every repository file it opens for reading; it starts no process. That list is GENERATOR_SOURCES plus GENERATOR_DATA, and ExecutedSetTests re-derives it on every run, so a new import or read fails the tests until it is pinned. (2) The config: TAP's util/hotspot.config (read by the generator) and the frozen new_hotspot.config it becomes, which is one of (3) the inputs: each reference's frozen inputs (their SHA256SUMS digest) and raw layout hash, under references and calls. (4) The solver binary, by identity rather than by path (with -g its bytes depend on the build directory): each call hashes the private copy it executes, binds that hash and the build provenance in its signed receipt, and the gate admits only the binary with that hash. Not pinned: the validate-reference, gate and record code. What it decides (the predicate, tolerance, metric, references, calls, limits, accounting, operator key and anchor) is written into this manifest, so a change to any of it changes the manifest; edits anywhere else leave the manifest and every PASS intact. The interpreter and its standard library are the host's (each receipt records the Python version).
source.pin: only what the calls execute or read; validate-reference and the gate refuse a manifest that is not exactly what the tree generates
source.solver: by identity: the SHA-256 of the private copy each call executes, bound in its signed receipt with the build provenance; the gate admits only that binary
